passages.text:
I was once called Hadassah—unknown, unseen. Yet I was taken into the king’s house… and made queen. A crown upon my head, yet fear within my heart.
I concealed my kindred and my people, dwelling in quietness, unsure of mine own place, ever beholding, and ever in fear.

Then went there forth a decree, that my people should be utterly destroyed. Fear gat hold upon me, for I alone stood near unto the throne; yet might I not draw nigh unto the king, except I should adventure my life.

I tarried in my spirit. I was of a doubtful heart. I feared the silence, and the distance, and the great price of the way.

Nevertheless, a word moved within my soul—what if I were set in this place for this very hour?

Therefore I purposed to go in, though I trembled; I stepped forth into peril, trusting that I was not forgotten of the Most High. The God of mine people
The Queen: “Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” — Esther 4:14
